key_insight: MedCORE makes medical image diagnosis more interpretable by structuring predictions around explicit clinical criteria rather than direct image-to-label mapping.
clinical_relevance: By aligning image evidence with clinician-like reasoning and uncertainty-aware weighting, the approach could support safer, more transparent diagnostic decision support across multiple imaging tasks.
method: Decomposes each diagnosis into clinically defined criteria and localizes supporting image regions.
Uses multi-scale feature encoding plus a Graph Attention Network to model relationships among criteria.
Aligns criterion evidence with clinical text descriptors, visual prototypes, and uncertainty-calibrated aggregation.
evidence_signal: Validated on ISIC 2018, BUSI, and IDRiD, with reported performance of 89.2%/85.7%/96.4% AUC, 96.1%/95.2%/98.4% AUC, and 84.3%/80.2%/92.8% AUC respectively.
watch_item: The framework’s added complexity may make real-world deployment dependent on high-quality criterion annotations, robust localization, and careful clinical validation.
paper_title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis
